findings.evidence: `twoPoint` is `∑' n, ‖S.overlap n‖ ^ 2 * Real.exp (-(S.energy n * t))` (line 92), so `hZ` is `Summable (fun n => ‖S.overlap n‖ ^ 2)` = summability of the `t = 0` summand. The same file already takes the weaker time-local form in `sq_norm_overlap_le_twoPoint_mul_exp` (line 263-264) and `twoPoint_pos` (line 292-293): `hs : Summable fun n => ‖S.overlap n‖ ^ 2 * Real.exp (-(S.energy n * t))`.
findings.fix: Parameterise by a reference time: `hasSum_twoPoint {E} (hE : ∀ n, E ≤ S.energy n) {t₀ t} (hs : Summable fun n => ‖S.overlap n‖ ^ 2 * Real.exp (-(S.energy n * t₀))) (ht : t₀ ≤ t) : HasSum … (S.twoPoint t)` — same one-line proof via `aₙ e^{-Eₙt} = aₙ e^{-Eₙt₀} e^{-Eₙ(t-t₀)} ≤ aₙ e^{-Eₙt₀} e^{-E(t-t₀)}`. Correspondingly state `twoPoint_mul_exp_sub_le` as `S.twoPoint t * exp (E₀ * t) - ‖Z₀‖² ≤ (S.twoPoint t₀ * exp (E₀ * t₀) - ‖Z₀‖²) * exp (-(Δ * (t - t₀)))`, which is exactly the present statement at `t₀ = 0` (then `S.twoPoint 0 - ‖Z₀‖² = twoPointExcitedWeight n₀`).
findings.issue: `hZ : Summable fun n => ‖S.overlap n‖ ^ 2` is summability at `t = 0` (it is literally `C₂(0) < ∞`), the strongest point of the family, yet the conclusions only concern `t ≥ 0`. Same over-strong hypothesis in `twoPointExcitedWeight_nonneg` (170), `hasSum_twoPoint` (244), `hasSum_twoPoint_mul_exp` (255), `twoPoint_mul_exp_sub_le` (274), `tendsto_twoPoint_mul_exp` (301), `norm_threePoint_div_twoPoint_sub_le` (409), `tendsto_threePoint_div_twoPoint` (460). It excludes spectra whose state density grows (an infinite tower with `∑ₙ|Zₙ|² = ∞` but every `t > 0` convergent), i.e. the continuum setting Layer 0 targets.

findings.evidence: `threePointWeight` (line 124) carries no time dependence, and `hasSum_threePoint`'s proof (lines 353-357) bounds the summand by `threePointWeight O p * Real.exp (-(E * t))`, so the hypothesis is the undamped `t = τ = 0` sum; the damped version supports the identical `nlinarith` step with `t - τ ≥ s₀`, `τ ≥ τ₀`.
findings.fix: Assume summability at reference separations `s₀, τ₀ ≥ 0`: `Summable fun p => S.threePointWeight O p * Real.exp (-(S.energy p.1 * s₀)) * Real.exp (-(S.energy p.2 * τ₀))`, and conclude for `s₀ ≤ t - τ`, `τ₀ ≤ τ` with the remainder `K₃(s₀,τ₀) * (exp (-(Δ * (τ - τ₀))) + exp (-(Δ * (t - τ - s₀))))`; the present statements are the `s₀ = τ₀ = 0` case.
findings.issue: Same pattern for the three-point correlator: `hO : Summable (S.threePointWeight O)` is summability of `‖Z n‖ ‖O n m‖ ‖Z m‖` with no exponential damping, i.e. convergence at `t = τ = 0`, while the conclusions only concern `0 ≤ τ ≤ t`. Instances: `threePointExcitedWeight_nonneg` (176), `hasSum_threePoint` (347), `hasSum_threePoint_mul_exp` (361), `norm_threePoint_mul_exp_sub_le` (374), `norm_threePoint_div_twoPoint_sub_le` (409), `tendsto_threePoint_div_twoPoint` (460).

summary: Hypotheses are otherwise well-calibrated and the two-point/three-point developments are not duplicative, but the main results assume `Summable (fun n => ‖Z n‖²)` and `Summable (threePointWeight O)` — convergence of the correlators at zero time separation, the strongest member of the family — where summability at a reference time `t₀` suffices with the same proofs. The file itself already uses the weaker, time-local hypothesis in two lemmas.
